schoolReviews.review: Awesome experience for our son. Started in Kindergarten, and made it through 2nd grade before moving out of state. Such a wonderful community with plenty of parental involvement. Also great home school solution during the pandemic, and after school programs (when they were operational before the current situation).

My son Thomas when he was in first grade was identified with additional social and emotional needs. The assessment, multidisciplinary plan, and follow through were amazing. He is in second grade and improved 80% in my mind. He doesn't have panic attacks and has begun to make friends and feels part of his school. His confidence and grades are quite good.My daughter Erica has a teacher with 30 years experience who makes practical suggestions to help a normal child. At Olympic View we feel we are in great hands.

We transferred here from a high profile private school. Since my child has been at this school he has improved in every subject area dramatically. He came home from the first day proclaiming that he goes to a real, bully free school. Terrific parent support and stupendous teachers makes this school a gem.
Olympic View is a wonderful school. The staff really cares about your children and their education. This is a top notch school.
Parental and Teacher involvement is off the charts. I stopped by for the Valentine's Day party for kindergarten and there were 19 parents for a class of 26 students.

schoolReviews.review: We had high hopes and had heard great things prior to 2019 from other families. The school has changed drastically since then due to SPS policies, so any review that pre-dates 2019 is no longer accurate. After having two students attend this school, we decided to leave the district. Academically, the school has very low standards. I don’t think they read a single book in 8th grade English class or wrote a single essay. Many students have no respect for the teachers, and the teachers are too young and inexperienced to do anything about it, or they are hobbled by anti-discipline, pro-inclusion policies that give teachers few tools for addressing disruptive behavior. There are a few teachers at the school that are wonderful, especially in the science department, but I found the constant gaslighting and dishonesty from leadership to be exhausting. Now that we have spent a year in another public middle school, where there is honest communication and where the staff really do want to see students to be challenged and to reach their full potential, I realize just how terrible and toxic this school really is!! I think the difference is largely policy/leadership driven (not demographically driven).

Some classrooms were extremely HOT, others were too cold. The teachers constantly pick favorites and it’s clear. Teachers have ZERO respect for any of the students, I am a current high schooler at Nathan hale and used to go to JAMS. I got frequently bullied for being Chinese by other POC kids and they did nothing about it. I got pushed and picked at for the entire time I went there. Students outcasted me because I have audhd and learn differently. I hate this school with a burning passion, I’ve been pulled by the NECK OF MY HOODIE by teachers when I didn’t look in their direction. I’ve been sat far away from other students by most teachers because they said I was too disruptive. (I had simply been drawing) & The bathrooms are absolutely disgusting. They do not let you order food from outside sources for lunch even though on multiple occasions I’ve found HAIR, Mold, And bugs in my food. I ordered food with MY money and they kept it in the office until the end of the day.
I had good friends and there are nice people. Not everyone is bad but they seriously need to work on respecting my others and community because it is very toxic based off of my experience.

This school, compared to most others, is disastrous. When you're in the school you don't realize it, but the teachers (with a few exceptions) always scratch the surface of what's being taught and give homework that is laborious but serves no purpose. The teaching is ineffective and isn't interesting, and the teachers, along with the staff, can barely keep students in control more than half of the time.
I would call my 3 years at this school amazing, not just for learning, but also for building friendhships.
Everything was fine at the school until my child needed help, then it was awful and we felt alone and ignored.

JAMS is a very good middle school. Most of my kids’ teachers have been good to excellent. We did have to address a bullying incident but the administration was very responsive. There are plenty of sports and after school activities.

schoolReviews.review: Nathan Hale High school is one of the most impeccable high schools in overall Seattle city. The best thing about this school are the teachers and the facilities. It’s diverse environment close to nature doesn’t give you the feel that you are actually living in the city. The school’s admission process is rigorous due to the competition ensuring only the best out of the best are admitted!
Unfortunately, this school is not safe anymore.

We were happy to send our daughter to a racially and economically diverse school (the next nearest high school is anything but), and the teachers are really great. They create a culture of acceptance and inclusion. The only unfortunate issue that the school does actually have control over is that the front desk and administrative staff that help students and parents are...not nice. At all. They don't seem to be happy with their jobs and are unable to just reach the bare-minimum of friendly.
The teachers are 100% committed to making learning relevant and accessible. The atmosphere is positive and accepting.

As a freshmen I was scared going to hale, I thought it was a gang school and a lot of my friends were going to Roosevelt so I was worried about socializing. My opinion immediately changed and I suddenly had a great group of friends both from the school volleyball team and just meeting people in class. The teachers are all so nice but they still push us to be the best we can. I know hale has a different curriculum than most schools and it does make a difference. In 9th grade having block classes made homework management a lot easier and yet I feel like I learned more than I have ever before . Everyone was so friendly, the upperclassmen were not scary at all and the overall vibe of the school is so positive.Amazing place, I feel really lucky to go here

I personally like this school. I'm currently coming back as a junior, and my experience as a sophomore was quite exceptional. I wasn't pleased with the freshman that year, too many annoying freshmen cliques. I sincerely hope that the incoming freshmen this school year are gonna be at least a bit better than the freshmen last school year, but hearing that most kids are coming from Eckstein, I highly doubt any improvement is gonna happen. I agree there are at least a handful of students suffer from marijuana use but I know for sure that half of them have quit their habits. So drug use won't be a huge issue. Most of the teachers know what their doing and are familiar in their field. My freshman history teacher, Teacher Ted, being a Harvard grad and all, is AMAZING at his field. As a former student of his, I found his class quite challenging, and I love it. There are a ton of other teachers who are quite similar to him, as well. The counseling is superb as well. I know kids who suffered depression and got help from the counselors and the school nurse, and the outcome was incredible. They are now more positive and joyful. Hale is an amazing school, despite the annoying freshies.

My daughter finished her freshman year at Hale this spring, and our entire family was pleasantly surprised by the school s quality. Because Hale doesn't have the academic reputation as its neighbor a few miles south, we were concerned our APP-qualified daughter wouldn't be challenged enough; but in talking with friends whose kids attend the "other" school as well as other parents at Hale, we feel the culture and curriculum at Hale were probably MORE challenging and stimulating (critical thinking is emphasized and interdisciplinary work is commonplace). We have heard graduates laud Hale for its ability to prepare students for college, and we now understand why this might be the case. Our daughter did have a couple of marginal teachers, but the rest were good to excellent, and the marginal ones were receptive to feedback. Beyond academics, we LOVE that Hale faculty and administration work hard to develop a culture of respect and appreciation for differences. Sure, some cliquishness remains, but it seems to be less than at other schools. On most days my daughter comes home excited about school and life, and she has even reported being proud of [her] school multiple times.

schoolReviews.review: Both my daughters attend this school. It is without question the best school in the district and is consistently ranked #1 in the state. The teachers and staff are phenomenal. The community is welcoming and most families volunteer in some capacity. The students are excited to learn, collaborate, and get creative. The school climate is supportive, welcoming, and inclusive. Cascadia currently houses the district's "Highly Capable" program for grades 2-5. It also houses a preschool program. (The school district has said it will eventually move some general education students into the school, but has not announced when that will happen.) The school has a much more diverse student population than most other North Seattle public schools and the school's Culture Night is a highlight of the year. Cascadia parents also host science fairs, talent shows, harvest fests, game nights, family camping trips, etc. The one significant negative is that the district does not allow the school to provide many Special Education services which means many 2E (twice exceptional) kids are not able to attend.

I went to Cascadia from 1-5th grade and absolutely loved it. Great atmosphere, very supportive teachers, challenging work, not much homework, overall an amazing experience. I made a lot for friends there and over the 5 years I was there, there was not a single problem with bullying that I know of.

I went here from 1st - 5th grade and it was amazing! Beautiful old building, and the outdoor space was used effectively. Nobody was ostracized by a teacher or bullied in my time there, and everything was kept new and exciting, so it was easy to pay attention (generally).We did a lot of fun projects and I learned a ton!Class sizes were also good, never too many or not enough people.

schoolReviews.review: Estoy muy agradecida con esta escuela, maestros y personal por todo el apoyo que le dieron a mis hijos, especialmente a mi hijo con educación especial, mis hijos los extrañan mucho.Está escuela la recomiendo al 100 verenize y cesar Escobar
Very supportive. Great at everything. Extremely fun. Highly recommend.

This school is ok compared to others. But it's not great. Some teachers care about your wellbeing and support you, while others do not care about your needs or your wellbeing. If you have social anxiety, or fear of big crowds this school will be hard for you. The school lunches also lack basic needs. The homework often feels useless, and the teachers lack to find roots of problems and take care of them properly. The school neglects some things.

its a great school! And the marching band is amazing even when it is rainy and cold these students will give it there all and I belive the amazing teachers have taught this amazing skill! The sports may not be the best overall but the coaches and community make it such a fun experience to be apart of! This school offers many extra-cirrucuals including theater which I would very highly recommend you see and many music programs recently adding a choir, also we have an amazing orchestra and 2 jazz bands, along with the 3 concert bands! We have high school level math classes all the way up to geometry! And also we have Japanese and Spanish classes that are great and immersive and give you high school credits. Since recently 6th graders cannot take a language but 7th grade and 8th grade will have an amazing time, while also having a Costa Rica trip for Spanish classes that u sign up for, and a Japan trip for Japanese class that you sign up for, while also having a DC trip that any 8th grader can sign up for. The whole school has an amazing community in general with all the fun activities you do during the school day! And all 8th graders get to go to a fun overnight trip at orkila and others grades have fun overnights as well! Overall this school is a fun inclusive environment for everyone!
This a wonderful, inclusive, slayful school that slayzzz

My child has loved their time at Robert Eagle. He has had great teachers thoughout 6-8, and the teachers have generally gone above and beyond to invest and connect with the kids vs just reciting from a text book. The school also has really great facilities (since it is a new school), has good diversity, and a strong principal.

In general I would recommend Eagle Staff to students who can work semi-independently and don’t feel too overwhelmed around many people. Teachers don’t try too hard to connect with individual students, probably because there are so many, so being able to regulate your own learning at times can be important. Also there are a lot of people so it does feel crowded sometimes, like in the cafeteria or during passing periods.Fairly good sports though.

schoolReviews.review: Absolutely love this school. It's small but mighty with amazing community, curriculum and enrichment programs. Would 100% recommend this school.

My daughters attend St Catherine and as a family, we feel well-cared for here. One of my children has significant problems with adhd and the school both detected her problems and have supported her. She is learning and loves her school and extra curricular activities. My other daughter has academic gifts and I trust the school to find ways to challenge her. We love participating with other parents and teachers/administrators to create an amazing experience for our children's mental, social, physical and spiritual learning. This community has supported our children and our family. We feel fortunate and blessed to be here. We recommend this school to other families who are looking for a close knit community

My child has been attending St. C. for a few years and we couldn’t be happier. It’s a small, sweet gem of a school and has been a breath of fresh air after attending a local public school. We’ve been very pleased with the academics and the teachers/staff. What really makes St. C. shine, though, is the community. Parents are involved and organize many fun social events, and the children (pre-K through 8) know each other. I love that everyone is looking out for my kid and each other.

The principal of this school is extremely abrasive. She is new and it shows. A neighbor inquired about this school for her son who has ADHD - the principal told her he would not be a good fit for the school, without even meeting him or seeing his school records. My daughter struggled socially and the school was no help. Class sizes are very large - my daughter's 2nd grade class had 28 students. Not worth the money.

I currently have a first grader and a pre-schooler in St. Catherine's. My children are very different from one another but they both enjoy the school, activities, teachers, staff, and curriculum. The school work is meaningful and rigorous enough without being overly time-consuming. There is a strong sense of community that pervades the school and all feel welcomed whether they are a member of the parish or not. Our family enjoys the company of the other families that attend the school and the school does a fantastic job bringing everyone together through year-round activities and functions. We are thrilled to have discovered this jewel in NE Seattle and look forward to our children attending many happy years at St. Catherine School.

I toured this school and am sharing information I found helpful in finding the right school for my kid, but have not had direct experience as a student/parent at this school. First of all, the director of Seattle campus is very friendly and welcoming, has good communication and shares personal interests to help connect with the students. The campus is clean, bright and spacious. The teachers work in offices with doors that shut so they have a private space for working 1-1 with students. There is a computer lab and space for lunch. The location is fun for teens, walking distance to eateries, etc. However, the teachers follow a prescribed curriculum that has been adapated by Brightmont corporate, and is applied across all campuses. Teachers are paid by the class, apparently, with zero prep time and zero time for communicating with parents. So there is little time to truly customize the curriculum. Homework is built into the curriculum, and can be integrated into the class itself but then the class it takes longer to complete because the curriculum cannot be customized. All parent communication goes through the site manager, and then to the teachers. Ratings by teachers on GlassDoor.com report that teachers are not employed full-time, and have no healthcare, making a high turn-over rate as teachers see this school as a step on their path to full-time employment. However, teachers are generally happy with the environment. While not right for my kid, this could be a good place for students who just need 1-1 attention, and are capable of following a standard curriculum.

Brightmont has been a light in the darkness for our family. Our daughter was struggling with doing all of her schooling online with Seattle Public Schools during the pandemic. She said she didn't feel connected to the material. Her grades and self esteem were plummeting. I spoke with a number of her peers who were having a similar experience. They all reported that they didn't feel like they were learning much in the public school remote learning environment. Signing her up at Brightmont has been a fantastic decision. She is back to actually learning again, and a bonus is that she really likes her teachers. Her confidence in her ability to learn, and be successful in school has also returned. I have been very pleased with the administration. They have been kind, accommodating, and very responsive to our communications and needs. My expectations are exceeded, especailly knowing how busy they must be! The school is doing a great job with covid precautions. I feel safe when my daughter attends in person. She also has the option for working remotely online. Attending in person gives her some social interaction where before she had had none. I highly recommend this school.
